data.description:
# Thruster hum Tone.js shim

## Goal

Implement the continuous, thrust-driven thruster hum as a lightweight Tone.js runtime shim, since baked WAV variants cannot reproduce a pitch/gain-continuous, thrust-coupled loop.

As the game's developer, I want the thruster hum to remain continuous and thrust-driven, so the tuning slider stays audible and the hum stays in lockstep with the flame animation.

## Scope

- Add a small Tone.js-based runtime shim that owns only the thruster hum; all other cues are baked assets (decision recorded on the parent epic).
- Preserve the existing `updateThrusterSound(level)` / `stopThrusterSound()` contract consumed by `Player.preUpdate`.
- Reproduce the documented character: triangle fundamental ~60 Hz + sine undertone ~35 Hz + band-pass filtered noise (700–1100 Hz) whoosh, gain ≤ 0.075.
- Mirror the flame growth/shrink timing (30 ms growth, ~4x decay) and avoid clicks on retrigger.
- Stop cleanly on release, respawn, player destroy and scene shutdown so no audio nodes leak.
- Degrade to a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- Add Tone.js as a pinned runtime dependency and verify it is the only new browser runtime dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The thruster hum is continuous while thrust is held and stops cleanly on release/respawn/destroy/scene shutdown.
- Hum gain tracks `getEngineSoundLevel` and stays ≤ 0.075.
- No clicks on retrigger; growth/decay match the documented flame timing.
- The shim is a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- No audio nodes leak after repeated thrust start/stop cycles (asserted in tests).
- Tone.js is pinned and is the only new browser runtime dependency introduced.
- `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.

## Dependencies

- Audio playback contract tests.
- Rewrite effects.ts to Phaser playback.

## Deliverables

- Thruster hum shim module.
- Wiring from `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` to the shim.
- Shim tests covering continuous gain tracking, clean stop and no-op degradation.

## Key Files

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` delegate here.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — per-frame driver.
- `src/core/movement.ts` — `getEngineSoundLevel` source.
- `package.json` — Tone.js dependency.
data.title: Thruster hum Tone.js shim

data.description:
## Problem

The global implement skill's parent phase (`implement.py parent`) has two gaps that cause epics to loop when a child is externally blocked:

1. **`do-not-delegate` is not honoured.** The herdr dispatcher respects the `do-not-delegate` tag, but `implement.py parent` does not: `_classify_child` returns "implement" for any non-terminal, non-in-progress child and `_next_child_to_implement` selects it regardless of the tag. An epic whose only startable child is guard-tagged will therefore be repeatedly selected and its guarded child re-attempted on every dispatch.

2. **Stale worktree branches are not reused or cleaned.** `git_worktree_add` runs `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <path> <parent>`, which fails if `<branch>` already exists. When a prior `start` aborted after creating the branch but before/at worktree removal, the branch survives and every subsequent `start` fails with a cryptic "Failed to create worktree" error instead of reusing the branch or reporting the stale branch clearly.

Observed on **Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge (AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J)** (session herdr-1791234333-893049-2032): `implement.py parent` selected the externally-blocked, `do-not-delegate` child **Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51)** and then failed worktree creation because the branch `wl-AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51-author-game-specific-toneforge-recipes` already existed.

## Expected behaviour

- `implement.py parent` skips `do-not-delegate` children (reports them as guarded/not startable) unless explicitly overridden.
- `git_worktree_add` either reuses an existing branch that is identical to / fast-forwardable from the parent branch, or fails with an actionable message naming the stale branch and how to recover.
- A failed `start` should not leave a stale branch behind (or should clean it up on abort).

## Scope

- Global implement skill script `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `git_worktree_add`, `phase_start`/abort path). This is agent-infrastructure code; report/plan changes there, do not edit from an AI_Hell worktree.
